newsitem.title: HONG KONG: South Korea recognises Hong Kong passport.
newsitem.headline: South Korea recognises Hong Kong passport.

text.p: South Korea, in a new boost for Hong Kong just 33 days before Britain hands it back to China, on Thursday joined the growing list of countries granting easy access for holders of the territory's future passport.
The Hong Kong government said Seoul had agreed to grant Hong Kong people visa-free entry for visits of up to 15 days.
The gesture "signified the strong commitment of Korea to Hong Kong's continued success and reaffirmed the world-class status of the passport", a spokesman said.
The move is reciprocal. Koreans currently can enter Hong Kong visa-free for visits of up to two weeks.

A string of countries, including Britain, the United States, Australia, Canada, Singapore, Japan, Thailand, the Philippines, Turkey and West Samoa, have recognised the post-handover passport and announced favourable entry conditions ranging from easy visas to completely visa-free access.
At midnight on June 30, Hong Kong becomes a "special administrative region" of China after 156 years of British rule.
